text: βαθμός, a step (of a stairway); hence, a stage in a career, a position.
βάθος (a) depth; (b) a depth, a deep (also met.).
βαθύνω, I deepen.
βαθύς, deep (lit. and met.); ὄρθρου βαθέως, in the depths of the early morning, while still very early.
βαΐον, a palm branch.
Βαλαάμ (Hebr.) (Balaham), Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament.
gloss: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates

text: Βαλάκ (Hebr.), Balac, Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab.
gloss: Balac, Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab

text: βαλλάντιον, a purse.
βαπτισμός, dipping, washing (of a ceremonial character).
βάπτω, (a) I dip; (b) I dye; Rev. xix 13, cf. δίβαφα, twice-dyed garments.
Βαράκ (Hebr.), Barak, one of the Judges of Israel.
gloss: Barak, one of the Judges of Israel

text: Βαραχίας (Hebr.), Barachias, Baruch. His identity is uncertain, perhaps father of the Zacharias killed by the Zealots in the last Jewish War (Josephus, B.J. iv 5. 4). See Ζαχαρίας.
βάρβαρος, a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin: as adj. foreign.
gloss: a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin

text: βαρέω, I weight, load, burden, lit. and met.
βαρέως, heavily, with difficulty.
Βαρθολομαῖος (Aram.)(son of Tholmai [=Ptolomaeus]), Bartholomew, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
gloss: Bartholomew, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus

text: Βαριησοῦς (Aram.), Bar-Jesus (i.e. son of Jesus), the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus. He is also called Elymas.
Βαριωνᾶς (Aram.), Bar-jonas, son of Jonas, the surname of Simon Peter.
βάρος, a weight, a burden, lit. or met.: in 1 Thess. ii 7 there may be a play on the derived sense, authority, dignity.
Βαρσαββᾶς (Aram.), Barsabbas, son of Sabbas, a surname of Joseph (Ac. i 23) and Judas (Ac. xv 22).
Βαρτίμαιος (Aram.), Bartimaeus, son of (?) Timaeus.
βαρύς, heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met.
βαρύτιμος, heavy in price, very expensive.
βασανισμός, torture.
βασανιστής, a torturer.
βάσανος, torture.

βασίλειος, (a) in Lk. vii 25 either masc. courtiers, or neut. palaces; (b) the LXX intended βασίλειον as subst., a body of kings, in the passage quoted by 1 Pet. ii 9, but Peter clearly takes βασίλειον as adj., royal.
βασίλισσα, a queen.
βάσις (properly, that on which something may rest), a foot.
βασκαίνω, I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower.
gloss: I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower

text: βάτος, a thorn-bush: ἐπὶ τοῦ (Lk. τῆς) βάτου, in the passage about the thorn-bush, Mk. xii 26, Lk. xx 37.
βάτος (Hebr.), a batus, a liquid measure among the Jews, containing 72 sextarii, that is, between eight and nine gallons.
gloss: a batus, a liquid measure among the Jews

text: βάτραχος, a frog.
βατταλογέω, I chatter, am long-winded, utter empty words.
gloss: I chatter, am long-winded, utter empty words

text: βδέλυγμα, an abominable thing, an accursed thing.
gloss: an abominable thing, an accursed thing

text: βδελυκτός, abominable, detestable.
βδελύσσομαι, I abominate, detest.
βεβαίωσις, confirmation, ratification, establishment.
βεβηλόω, I profane.

Βεεζεβούλ, Βεελζεβούλ, Beezebul, Beelzebul, a name of uncertain derivation, the chief of evil spirits among the Jews. The form Beelzebub = god of Flies at Ekron (2 Kings i 2, 3): the better attested form perhaps = the Phoenician Sungod as lord of the heavenly dwelling.
Βελίαρ (originally a Hebrew word = uselessness, corruption), Beliar (spelt sometimes Belial, Beliab), a demon, among the Jews, and in fact a name for Satan.
gloss: Beliar (spelt sometimes Belial, Beliab), a demon

text: βελόνη, a needle.
βέλος, a missile, dart.
βέλτιον (very rare in this period), an adverb, comparative in form, superlative in meaning, best.
Βενιαμείν (Hebr.), Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Βερνίκη, Berenice (Lat.), (born A.D. 29) daughter of Agrippa I and Kypros, and sister of M. Iulius Agrippa II, in whose company she appears, Ac. xxv, xxvi.
Βέροια, Beroea, a town of the province Macedonia.
gloss: Beroea, a town of the province Macedonia

text: Βεροιαῖος, belonging to Beroea, Beroean.
Βηθλεέμ, Bethlehem, a town of Judaea.
Βηθσαϊδά, Bethsaida, a city of Galilee.
Βηθφαγή, Bethphage, a village in the neighbourhood of Jerusalem, on the Mt. of Olives.
gloss: Bethphage, a village in the neighbourhood of Jerusalem

text: βήρυλλος, a beryl, a precious stone of various colours, the best known being sea-green.
gloss: a beryl, a precious stone of various colours

text: βία, force.
βιάζομαι, (a) mid. I use force, I force my way, I come forward violently, cf. Mt. xi 12 (where perhaps pass.); (b) pass. I am forcibly treated.
gloss: I use force, I force my way, I come forward violently

text: βίαιος, strong, violent.
βιαστής, a forceful, violent man.
βιβλαρίδιον, a little papyrus roll.
βιβρώσκω, I eat.
Βιθυνία, Bithynia, a Roman province, NW. of Asia Minor and SW. of the Black Sea.
βιόω, I live.
βίωσις, manner of life.
βιωτικός, belonging to ordinary life, with somewhat contemptuous attitude.
βλαβερός, injurious.
βλάπτω, I injure.
βλαστάνω, βλαστάω, intr. I sprout: tr. I cause to sprout, make to grow up, James v 18.
Βλάστος, Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I.
gloss: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I

text: βλάσφημος, abusive, scurrilous.
βλέμμα, look, the faculty of looking.
βλητέον (verbal adj. from βάλλω): sc. ἐστίν, one must put.
Βοανηργές, Boanerges, a doubtful name of doubtful origin and meaning: see my crit. note.
βοή, a shout.
βοήθεια, (a) abstr., assistance; (b) concr. (a technical term of nautical language), a help.
βοηθέω, I come to the rescue of, come to help, help.
gloss: I come to the rescue of, come to help, help

text: βοηθός, helper.
βόθυνος, a hole in the earth, ditch.
gloss: a hole in the earth, ditch

text: βολή, a casting, throw: in acc. as measure of distance.
βολίζω, I cast the line (for sounding), I sound.
gloss: I cast the line (for sounding), I sound

text: Βοός, Βοές (Hebr.), Boos or Boes (Boaz), son of Salmon (Sala) and Rahab, husband of Ruth, father of Iobed.
gloss: Boos or Boes (Boaz), son of Salmon (Sala) and Rahab

text: βόρβορος, a miry dungeon. hole.
note: The mark between "dungeon" and "hole" looks like a full stop on the image (possibly a broken hyphen, "dungeon-hole"); transcribed as a full stop. | approved by David, 2026-11-09

text: βορρᾶς, the north wind, hence the north.
βόσκω, I feed.
Βοσόρ, Bosor, father of Balaam: but see Βεώρ.
βοτάνη, fodder, food.
βότρυς, cluster (bunch) of grapes.
βουλεύομαι, I deliberate, take counsel.
βουλευτής, a member of a βουλή (city council), in N. T. of the συνέδριον, Sanhedrin at Jerusalem.
gloss: a member of a βουλή (city council)

text: βούλημα, will, desire.
βουνός (tumulus), a hillock, hill.
βοῦς, an ox.
βραβεῖον, a prize.
βραβεύω, I decide (in a conflict between contending forces); hence, I rule, I administer.
βραδύνω, I am slow, I delay: followed by gen., 2 Pet. iii 9.
βραδυπλοέω, I sail slowly.
βραδύς, slow.
βραδυτής, tardiness, dilatoriness.
βραχίων, arm.
βραχύς, little: mostly in various adverbial phrases, indicating degree or time.
βρέφος, infant, babe, bantling, child in arms: ἀπὸ βρέφους, from babyhood (cf. a pueris).
gloss: infant, babe, bantling, child in arms

text: βρέχω, (a) I wet; (b) I rain, having originally the raingod (Ζεύς, Jupiter) as subject (cf. Mt. v 45 and Latin pluo): thence, of a shower from the sky other than rain, Lk. xvii 29.
note: "rain-god" is broken across a line end; joined as "raingod" (cf. Souter's "Sungod" under Βεεζεβούλ).

text: βροχή, a wetting, rain.
βρόχος, a noose.
βρυγμός, gnashing, crunching.
βρύχω, I gnash, crunch.
βρύω, I cause to gush forth, send forth.
gloss: I cause to gush forth, send forth

text: βρώσιμος, eatable, suitable for food.
βυθίζω, I cause to sink.
βυθός, the deep sea.
βυρσεύς, a tanner.
βύσσινος, of fine-linen, of lawn.
βύσσος (Semitic origin), fine-linen. (Some authorities consider cotton to be meant; others silk.)
βωμός, an altar.

Γαββαθά, Gabbatha, i.e. Gab Baitha, ‘the ridge (back) of the House’, i.e. the Aramaic name for what the Greeks called Λιθόστρωτον, a sort of paved square, on which the procurator had his judgement seat.
Γαβριήλ (Hebr.), Gabriel, a messenger of God.
γάγγραινα, a cancerous sore, a cancer.
Γάδ (Hebr.), Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
gloss: Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel

text: Γαδαρηνός, Gadarene, belonging to Gadara (an important Hellenized town, one of the Decapolis, and SE. of the Sea of Galilee), see Γερασηνός, Γεργεσηνός.
γάζα (a Persian loan-word), treasure.
γαζοφυλάκιον, treasury.

Γάϊος, Gāïus, (a) a Corinthian, Rom. xvi 23, 1 Cor. i 14; (b) a Macedonian (?), Ac. xix 29; (c) a citizen of Derbe, Ac. xx 4; (d) an Ephesian (?), 3 John 1. It may be that (b) and (c) or even (b), (c), and (d) are identical.
γάλα, milk.
Γαλάτης, a Galatian (meaning any inhabitant of the Roman province Galatia).

Γαλατία, Galatia, a large Roman province in central Asia Minor, comprising the districts of Paphlagonia, Pontus Galaticus, Galatia (in the narrower sense, which some still think is intended in the N.T.), Phrygia Galatica, Lycaonia Galatica, Pisidia and Isaurica. In 2 Tim. iv 10 the reference may be to Gaul, even if we read Γαλατίαν.
gloss: Galatia, a large Roman province in central Asia Minor

text: Γαλατικός, Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia: τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν, Ac. xvi 6, ‘the region which is both Phrygian (racially) and Galatic (by administration)’.
gloss: Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia

text: γαλήνη, a calm.

Γαλλίων, Gallio, Lucius Iunius Gallio, who received this name by adoption into another family, but was born brother of the philosopher Seneca and originally named L. Annaeus Nouatus; proconsul of the Roman province Achaia from spring A.D. 52 to spring 53.
Γαμαλιήλ (Hebr.), Gamaliel, a noted Pharisee, teacher of Saul.
gloss: Gamaliel, a noted Pharisee, teacher of Saul

text: γαμίζω, I give in marriage: this sense probably even in 1 Cor. vii 38, where the older view took it as equal to γαμέω.
γαμίσκομαι, I am given in marriage (reading doubtful).
γαστήρ, belly: often ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν, of a woman, to be pregnant (lit. to have [a child] in the belly).
Γεδεών (Hebr.), Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel.
gloss: Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel

text: Γεθσημανεί, Gethsemani, a small place between the brook Kidron and the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem.
γείτων, a neighbour.
γελάω, I laugh.
γέλως, laughter.
γεμίζω, I fill, load.
γενεαλογέομαι, I am put into a genealogy.
gloss: I am put into a genealogy

text: γενεαλογία, genealogy.
γενέσια, birthday-anniversary feast.
γενετή, birth.
γέννημα (from γεννάω), of animal, never of vegetable, products (contrast γένημα), offspring, child.
Γεννησαρέτ, Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias, which was in consequence sometimes called the Lake of Gennesaret.
gloss: Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias

text: γεννητός, begotten, used as subst.
Γερασηνός, Gerasene, of Gerasa, a town on the E. of the Lake of Tiberias. Wherever this people is mentioned, the variants Γαδαρηνός and Γεργεσηνός occur.

γερουσία, the assembly or body of elders, probably as synonymous with or explicative of συνέδριον and πρεσβύτεροι. (The term γερουσία was often used in such a collective sense in the cities of Asia Minor, cf. Ramsay, Cities and Bishoprics of Phrygia, vol. i, p. 64.)
gloss: the assembly or body of elders

text: γέρων, an old man.
γεωργέω, I work the soil, I cultivate the soil.
gloss: I work the soil, I cultivate the soil

text: γεώργιον, a cultivated field.
γῆρας, old age.
γηράσκω, I become old, grow old.
γλεῦκος, sweet wine, made perhaps from a small specially sweet grape.
γλυκύς, sweet.
γλωσσόκομον (a vernacular word), bag, purse: some prefer to take as box, chest.
γναφεύς, fuller.
γνήσιος (lit. born), hence real, true, genuine; τὸ γνήσιον, the true, genuine element.
γνησίως, truly, genuinely; honourably.
γνόφος, darkness.
γνώστης, a knower, expert.
γογγύζω, I whisper, murmur, grumble (generally of smouldering discontent).
γογγυσμός, murmuring, grumbling.
γογγυστής, murmurer, grumbler.
γόης, a conjuror, juggler, sorcerer; a tricky (crafty) deceiver, impostor.
Γολγοθά, Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem.
gloss: Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem

text: Γόμορρα, Gomorrha, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea.
gloss: Gomorrha, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea

text: γόμος, a cargo, freight.
